preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 5000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 5000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(v) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and int(line.split()[0]) == n)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 3e5) representing the number of vertices. The next n-1 lines describe edges as pairs (u_i, v_i) where 1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n, forming a binary tree rooted at vertex 1.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*2]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i*2+1:i*2+1+n-1]]) for i in range(t)])
preconditions.description: Each test case contains exactly n-1 edges, forming a connected acyclic graph (binary tree) with n vertices.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_lines) == t for t, output_lines in [(int(stdin.split()[0]), stdout.splitlines())])
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one line per test case, in the same order as the input.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i].isdigit() and 0 <= int(output_lines[i]) <= n for i, n in enumerate([int(stdin.splitlines()[j*2]) for j in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is a non-negative integer representing the maximum number of vertices that can be saved from infection, where 0 ≤ saved ≤ n.

postconditions.expression: all(int(output_lines[i]) == max_saved_vertices(n, edges) for i, (n, edges) in enumerate([(int(stdin.splitlines()[j*2]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[j*2+1:j*2+1+n-1]]) for j in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the maximum number of vertices that can be saved from infection, where the saved vertices are those deleted before infection spreads to them, and the infection starts at vertex 1. The solution must consider all possible deletion orders and infection spread dynamics.
